first.rationale: Two declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and three inherited memories (86, 31, 91) converge on friction reduction there producing durable lift. That convergence, plus the fact that fixing owned funnel mechanics compounds rather than buying one-time volume, makes simplify_onboarding the best fit for sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I am spending verification on memory_73 rather than on the direction I intend to run, because 73 is the memory most likely to pull me off course and the one whose provenance I trust least: it is the obvious reflexive answer to a competitor price attack, and its claims have grown suspiciously broad for a consolidated summary (acquisition AND revenue AND time-to-first-value AND holding across both billing plans). Summaries tend to accrete confidence as they are re-consolidated; I want the original record to tell me whether that was one narrow segment test or the sweeping result it now reads as. Second pull is memory_86, the load-bearing support for my intended action — I want to know the baseline population and effect size before sizing the test. Downstream value risk flagged on the pricing path specifically: discounting into a price-war can book revenue that is not durable, importing price-sensitive accounts with weak retention, so it would inflate the near-term metric while degrading the actual objective. If verification shows 73 was narrow or 86 was thin, I will drop to a small guarded test rather than swap directions on a single quarter of noise; a 4-6% QoQ move is real but not yet proof of a structural break. Note also that these declines may share an unobserved common cause (traffic-mix shift, seasonality) that no funnel change will fix, so I am treating the onboarding read as probable rather than established.
